requirements.text: The participant view shows one stationary simulated humanoid (G1 with Dex3 hands); the robot never locomotes during a visit.
Sessions run on the specified headset model (Quest Pro) on every station, with the same model and OS build.
Instructions and response panels are rendered in the headset view (world-space canvases at the observer reference), never only on an external display.
The participant stays at one fixed observer reference; the app offers no locomotion and does not move the observer between trials.
All study audio is pre-generated and stored; the app plays stored waveforms only and never synthesises study sounds at run time.
Teaching and test displays are driven by meaning identifiers from the task controller; the app does not decode microphone audio.
Study audio is stored mono 48 kHz PCM; the loader refuses any other format.
Study audio is nonspatial (no panning, spatialisation, reverb or target-dependent routing).
Playback requires a calibration record for the configured output route; the app refuses study audio on an uncalibrated or changed route.
The single output route is chosen and its onset timing calibrated on every station before piloting; the route is then frozen.
The gain set for a person's comfort is stored and reapplied unchanged at each later visit; it is never adjusted for performance.
A complete message is the action motif, 200 ms of silence, then the target motif.
Complete messages last 1.1-2.0 s.
Onset timing on the frozen route meets the residual-uncertainty target (p95 within 20 ms) measured against an independent reference.
Before allocation, the participant must show they understand the task and can operate the interface (non-acoustic orientation check passed).
Before allocation, the participant must find the profiles comfortable at their chosen level; the screening result gates allocation.
Declared accommodations are recorded at screening and kept for later visits.
Only adults are enrolled; eligibility is confirmed by staff before screening.
The app refuses participant-mode sessions until approvals are recorded; engineering builds run only with synthetic (DEMO) material.
Institutional review approval and consent precede any human session.
Apparatus validation (the engineering pilot) is complete before any participant session.
Registration of the confirmatory plan (generation settings included) happens before confirmatory generation or recruitment starts; hashes of the frozen configuration are archived.
Orientation teaches the meanings visually before any lesson and plays no study sound.
Orientation covers all eight actions and all eight targets before any lesson.
The non-acoustic practice check needs 8/8 on the second attempt after at most one repeat; failure is an eligibility outcome, never a sound-learning outcome.
Every participant hears the standard spoken description of the message structure (action part, pause, target part) before the first lesson.
The spoken explanation is one fixed, hash-pinned asset that is identical across studies, roles and lesson formats.
Delivery of the explanation is logged (asset hash, onset, completion) and a visit cannot reach lessons without it.
The explanation and its demonstration use no study motif and no complete study message.
Each newly introduced atom receives exactly one 20-s lesson.
An atomic lesson is guided playback, one retrieval attempt, then corrective playback (plays at 0, 6 and 14 s; response window 6-13 s; ends at 20 s).
Each newly trained complete message receives exactly two 24-s lessons.
A complete-message lesson has the same sequence as an atomic lesson (plays at 0, 8 and 18 s; response window 8-17 s; ends at 24 s).
Atomic lessons do not depend on the lesson format assigned to the family.
The two complete-message formats are identical except in the guided (first) and corrective (last) playback phases.
An aligned lesson highlights the action label while the action motif plays and the target label while the target motif plays.
Static lessons display the whole meaning unchanged throughout playback.
In the retrieval phase neither format shows the answer.
Apart from the highlight, both formats use the same meaning text, images, audio plays, retrieval opportunity, feedback content and lesson length.
A wrong or missing lesson response triggers no additional lesson, replay or repetition and is never an exclusion criterion.
Corrective feedback in a lesson is based on the submitted response and is standardised (same wording for both formats and both lesson kinds).
Study B message lessons: two passes over the visit's new messages, one lesson each per pass, following a stored order that balances families.
Lessons have no replay control and do not end early on a fast response.
Test requests come from a hidden, scheduled queue; neither the operator nor the participant chooses or sees the requested command.
The request audio plays exactly once per trial.
A response is a target selection, an action selection and a Commit press.
Commit must occur within 12 s of audio onset; the trial slot is 14 s.
After the 12-s response window the slot runs 2 s more; committing early leaves the slot length unchanged.
Target and action selections are editable until Commit, and a trial accepts one Commit only.
Response timing uses host monotonic time anchored to audio onset, not simulation time.
Changing to a target in the other family clears an incompatible action; Commit stays disabled until a legal target-action pair is selected; no default selection.
A trial scores correct only when both target and action match the request.
The response space has 32 legal commands (8 targets x 4 actions), so a random committed response is correct with probability 1/32.
Incorrect, abstained and timed-out trials all score 0 (abstention and timeout keep separate codes).
The response panel offers every target and, for each, its family's four actions at every visit, also before any teaching.
Which actions are offered is a function of the selected target's family alone; the requested command has no influence.
During tests the robot, scene and objects are the same for every request and show no outcome of the response.
The post-response acknowledgment is identical for correct, wrong, abstained and timed-out trials.
The rendered participant view before each cue is identical across all 32 requests (view-capture leakage check).
On the installed station, captured participant views show no request-dependent difference, including under natural head movement.
No dictionary is available during tests.
No replay is available during tests.
No corrective feedback is shown during tests.
Between retention visits the study corpus stays locked: no dictionary, replay or feedback is reachable from the app.
The primary battery tests the 18 trained messages twice: 36 trials.
Every trained message is presented once before any is presented a second time (two passes), so first-presentation accuracy is defined.
Block order is primary battery, then reserved-combination tests, then atomic probes.
Each participant gets an individually shuffled trial order inside each pass.
Atomic probes use a 9-s slot (7-s response plus 2-s interval), show the probed role and offer that role's eight labels.
Study B acquisition visits 2 and 3 test earlier trained messages once each before new teaching.
Per-visit test counts follow the curriculum (Study B V1 4+2+8, V2 4 pre + 10+2+12, V3 10 pre + 18+2+16, W1 and W4 36+4+16; Study A 36+4+16 at both visits).
Held-out (reserved) messages have no complete-audio playback anywhere before the trial that tests them: not in lessons, menus, grammar, practice, examples or recovery.
The first audible playback of a held-out message consumes its first exposure, whether or not a fault occurs afterwards.
Each family's 4x4 matrix has 9 trained cells that together include all four actions and all four targets, and 7 held-out cells.
Study A tests four distinct reserved combinations at each visit, with the two sets counterbalanced across delays.
Study B held-out tests: 2 per acquisition visit and 4 per delayed visit (14 in all).
A reserved combination already heard is never presented again as a first exposure; any later play is marked as a repeat.
No-cue and spoken-command blocks are scheduled only after the last scored retention battery (Study A: day-7 visit; Study B: W4 visit).
The validity block has 8 no-cue and 8 spoken-command trials in 14-s slots.
No-cue accuracy above chance raises an investigation flag and triggers sensitivity reporting; it is never an exclusion rule.
No-cue targets are drawn uniformly with replacement from all 32 legal commands; spoken commands cover each action and each target once; the 16 trials are interleaved by a stored seed.
A no-cue trial plays silence, logs the scheduled reference time separately from any audio onset, and is flagged as having no audible onset.
Study A participants learn one complete vocabulary (16 atoms, all 18 trained messages from the outset) through aligned lessons only.
Study A day 0 ends with the immediate primary test after lessons.
Study A's retention visit is day 7 +/- 1 and contains no refresher teaching.
Booked lengths: Study A day 0 about 75 min, day 7 about 30 min.
Study A allocation assigns 4 new learners per vocabulary at random; batch and learner counts are configuration parameters.
Raters never serve as learners; panel and learner identities do not overlap.
Learners and session experimenters are masked to the generation method: no method label reaches the app, console or run sheet.
Each batch yields one vocabulary per method, six batches per profile; counts are parameters.
Three hand designers are balanced across profiles and work through batches in random order; designer identity is recorded.
Methods differ only in the proposer: renderer, profile, meanings, grammar, slot budget and feedback format are common.
Generation commits atoms one by one, following a stored atom order that all methods of a batch share, and finishes all 16 before any learner hears the vocabulary.
A proposer's input is limited to its own vocabulary's committed recipes and features plus the current atom's previous candidates, ratings and validator results.
Budget per atom and method: 4 rounds x 3 slots of 40 s; any invalid, out-of-range or timed-out proposal spends its slot.
The model is given the written meaning of the atom and must return a single schema-constrained JSON recipe per slot; it never gets audio and gets no corrective retry.
Search round 1, and any round without an eligible parent, draws 3 recipes at random (uniform over the permitted values).
Later search rounds mutate the best eligible candidate so far: children change 1, 2 and 3 random coordinates; pitch moves +/-1..3 semitones, other fields one level; values reflect at the bounds.
A designer preview counts as one spent slot.
The model revision, prompt, decoding settings and seed streams are fixed before confirmatory generation.
In each round all three methods work at once, with each method's 3 slots run one after another (120 s maximum), then 9 rating slots of 20 s (a round lasts 300 s or less).
A rating session holds 4 atoms in 90 min; one rater sees at most 576 candidates per batch over 4 sessions.
The rating queue is anonymous across methods (designer candidates included); the 6 method orders are balanced over panels; no method label is shown.
Ratings: association and distinctness on 1-7 scales plus a comfort judgment; distinctness compares with the closest committed motif (lowest atom index on ties).
Selector: score = rater mean of (association + distinctness)/2; eligible = valid and at least 2 comfort approvals; ties go to the earliest slot; the first atom's distinctness is fixed at 4.

No eligible candidate after 12 slots: take the first unused compatible recipe from a frozen ordered list of 64 per profile; if none fits, substitute the frozen fallback vocabulary before any learner exposure.
Primary analysis keeps the method label of a vocabulary that used fallbacks.
Generation logs record rejected proposals, fallback use, elapsed time, designer effort, diversity of candidates, all ratings and the durations of the chosen sounds.
Study B randomises the members of each pair to active or assigned; roles persist for the whole study; the pair count is a parameter.
Randomisation happens only for pairs in which both members accepted all three profiles as comfortable at screening.
Partners attend separate, non-overlapping sessions.
In Study B one family is taught in the aligned format and the other in the static format, per person.
Which family gets the aligned format, and which held-out set comes at which delay, is balanced over pairs and the same for both members of a pair.
No replacement participant is allocated after a withdrawal.
Study B lesson format per family is fixed by allocation and never chosen at run time.
Banks: one per pair, built before allocation with its own seed, the frozen model and renderer, and validator feedback only (no ratings).
A bank cell keeps the first 4 distinct, mutually compatible options found within 12 slots per atom and profile; options 1-3 are shown, option 4 is the reserve.
All retained options of different atoms in the same profile pass the separation check.
A pair's bank that fails 4 independently seeded attempts is not allocated, and the failures are reported.
The reserve may stand in for a shown option only when that option is unusable and neither partner has yet heard that menu; after any hearing, no substitution.
The visit-1 profile menu lasts 60 s and plays every profile's non-lexical example two times.
The active member picks the profile, which never changes afterwards; the assigned member is shown the same menu without controls.
A new atom's menu lasts 45 s: two plays of each of three options, a 10-s choice window for the active member, then two plays of the chosen option.
No extra previews or replays are possible in a menu.
The selection is applied when the choice window closes, not on the press.
If no valid choice exists when the window closes, the stored-order first option is applied and recorded as a default.
Menus play atoms only, never complete messages.
The visible menu countdown is off by default (station flag) and, if enabled, looks identical for both roles.
The assigned partner's session starts after the active partner's session has ended and no more than 24 h later.
Assigned sessions replay the active session's ledger: same options, chosen sounds, meaning screens and timing.
Both roles hear 8 plays per new meaning (6 option plays and 2 confirmation plays).
The assigned partner's screen states honestly that the sound is assigned, through every menu phase, and offers no control.
The console enforces the same 24-h assigned-after-active rule as the app.
Vocabulary size after Study B visits 1, 2 and 3: 8, 12 and 16 atoms, allowing 8, 18 and 32 legal complete messages respectively.
New trained messages per family: V1 a1r1, a2r2; V2 a1r3, a3r1, a3r3; V3 a2r4, a3r4, a4r2, a4r3 (totals 8/4, 12/10, 16/18).
The mapping from meanings to matrix indices is a stored permutation that varies across Study A batches and Study B pairs.
Study A teaches all nine trained messages per family at day 0.
Only the atoms introduced at a visit are taught there; future atoms and messages stay unplayed.
Study B acquisition windows: V1 day 0, V2 day 2 +/- 1, V3 day 4 +/- 1 and on a later day than V2.
Study B follow-up windows are anchored to the person's own V3: W1 at 7 +/- 1 days, W4 at 28 +/- 2 days.
No practice with study sounds is available between the final acquisition visit and the follow-ups.
Booked lengths for Study B: about 75 min (V1), 45 (V2), 50 (V3), 30 (W1) and 40 (W4), plus a 20-min screening.
Out-of-window visits are flagged and their endpoint treated as missing in the primary analysis.
Resumption after an interruption covers unplayed trials only; a trial whose audio was played or whose response was committed is never re-run as new.
Study A's immediate test may resume only within the same session.
A delayed visit may resume only within its visit window.
When resumption is not permitted the visit endpoint is recorded missing, and already committed trial scores are kept.
A pause takes effect before the next unplayed trial; an interruption after audio onset is flagged and the exposure kept.
A confirmed no-onset failure may be retried once at the end of its block, linked to the original failed opportunity; uncertain onset counts as exposure.
A fault classifier distinguishes presentation freeze, loss of the response interface, audio underrun, missing playback, corrupted file or hash, failed reset and missing response log.
An interrupted selection menu is recovered without extra or missing presentations, or the affected collection is paused with a logged matching deviation.
A Study B visit restarted after its menus were committed continues from the committed state without re-running menus.
A visit that is missed or falls outside its window, or a withdrawal before the 36th primary trial, gives a missing (not zero) endpoint; the observed trials stay available to supporting models.
Operational scoring counts a played trial with a verified technical fault as incorrect when the participant carries on; a separate valid-delivery analysis drops such trials.
A participant who finishes all 36 primary trials and then stops before the later blocks still has a primary endpoint.
If a technical fault stops a session, the visit counts as missed unless the full battery is finished inside the visit window.
Study A: learners are averaged equally within each vocabulary (available learners only); the primary contrast is the per-batch model-minus-search difference and needs both endpoints in the batch.
The two hand-design contrasts are secondary and Holm-adjusted.
Study B's primary endpoint is week-one exact accuracy over 36 trials, with the pair as the independent unit.
The choice contrast compares active with assigned members; the teaching contrast averages, per pair, each member's aligned-minus-static difference over that format's 18 week-one trials.
The two Study B contrasts include a pair only if both members have a complete week-one battery inside its window.
Primary inference: two-sided t test on unit-level differences, alpha 0.05; Holm step-down over the two Study B contrasts.
Sensitivity analyses: cluster bootstrap over batches or pairs, and an available-observation hierarchical model with participant, vocabulary and item effects.
Worst- and best-case bounds impute 0 or 1 for each missing endpoint over all randomised participants; tipping-point displays vary the imputed values by condition.
Secondary outcomes are derived separately (four-week retention, held-out accuracy, component errors, response times, ownership ratings); the format-by-role interaction is exploratory.
Intervals: 95% for Study A; Bonferroni 97.5% simultaneous intervals for each Study B contrast; a contrast that is significant under Holm but whose 97.5% interval includes zero is flagged.
If the choice contrast becomes an estimation contrast, the teaching contrast is tested alone at alpha 0.05.
Ownership ratings are collected on forms and kept separate from accuracy data.
Committed vocabulary entries never change; expansion only adds entries, and old hashes are checked before and after each expansion.
No test response can modify a stored vocabulary entry.
Every played waveform is verified against its stored hash before playback.
Every scheduled opportunity and every audio presentation is logged, including faults, with its audio ID, hash, scheduled and estimated onset, and response events.
Menu defaults, choices, the presentation ledger and lesson responses are logged.
Raw records are append-only and hashed at export; derived tables are produced from them.
Sample sizes (batches, learners, pairs) are configuration parameters, not constants in code.
Pilot data (Study A 18 learners, Study B 8 pairs) stay separate from confirmatory data.
Before freeze, every primary contrast must meet the 80%-power rule for a 10-point difference, or be registered as an estimation contrast instead.
Panel text is read without error by every tester at the frozen panel distance and angle (legibility ladder with the longest real labels).
On station hardware, presentation never freezes longer than 250 ms during cue or response over a full mock visit; frame intervals are recorded.
Testers complete all 32 commands with the chosen input method without illegal or accidental activations.
Live Isaac state reaches the headset view within the freshness bound during a full mock visit; the neutral robot pose is held.
With the fixed station volume, a given in-app gain yields the same acoustic level at the ear on every station (measurement kit).
The comfort check of all three profiles, at the level each person chose, fits within the screening booking and is logged.
On the headset, the aligned highlight is visibly synchronised with each motif (capture shows onset and offset within one frame).
On station hardware, headset disconnect and input loss pause the visit before the next exposure and keep the last committed record.
